EGY.hook: About 95% of Egyptians live on roughly 5% of the land — from orbit the inhabited country is a thin green ribbon along the Nile.
EGY.place: The northeast corner of Africa, with the Sinai peninsula reaching across into Asia.

DZA.hook: The largest country in Africa, and about four-fifths of it is Sahara — the population clings to the northern coast.
DZA.place: The middle of the Maghreb coast between Morocco and Tunisia, running deep south into the desert.

MAR.hook: You can stand on its coast and see Spain — the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 13km across at its narrowest.
MAR.place: The northwest corner of Africa, with both Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts and the Atlas range inland.

TUN.hook: Contains the northernmost point in Africa, and Carthage — Rome's great rival — stood just outside the modern capital.
TUN.place: The small wedge on the Mediterranean between Algeria and Libya, reaching closest to Sicily.

LBY.hook: The Great Man-Made River pumps fossil water from under the Sahara through 2,800km of pipe — the largest irrigation project ever built.
LBY.place: On the Mediterranean between Tunisia and Egypt, almost entirely desert behind a thin coastal strip.

SDN.hook: Has more pyramids than Egypt — around 200 of them at Meroë, steeper and narrower, and far less visited.
SDN.place: Below Egypt on the Red Sea, above South Sudan, where the Blue and White Niles meet at Khartoum.
